item.title: Yasukuni Shrine visits and offerings tear away Japan's "country for peace" mask
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Yasukuni Shrine visits and offerings tear away Japan's "country for peace" mask Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Oct. 17 sent a ritual offering, known as "masakaki," to the Yasukuni Shrine, a notorious shrine which honors convicted Japanese Class-A war criminals from World War II, under her title as prime minister, local media reported. She made a monetary offering to the shrine through senior officials of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party on Oct. 19. During Japan's "autumn festival," several Japanese politicians made offerings, while some cabinet ministers and lawmakers visited the shrine in person. By pressing ahead with offerings and visits despite repeated opposition from peace advocates at home and abroad, such erroneous acts desecrate historical justice, challenge the bottom line of human civilization, and constitute a provocation to the postwar international order. The Yasukuni Shrine has never been merely a religious site. It is a spiritual tool and symbol of the Japanese militarism that drove wars of aggression abroad. Recently, Japanese media released internal meeting records from the shrine for the first time, revealing the full decision-making process behind the enshrinement of 14 Class-A war criminals, including Hideki Tojo. The documents show that the Japanese government made arrangements on the enshrinement of Class-A war criminals with the shrine as early as the 1960s, but chose to keep the public in the dark until it was revealed in 1979. This revelation once again confirms that the Yasukuni Shrine is unequivocally a shrine to war criminals. The Japanese government at the time knew full well the disgrace of enshrining Class-A war criminals and, fearful of the consequences, deliberately kept the decision-making process secret. Fully aware that these war criminals were the chief culprits behind the Japanese militarists' war of aggression with the blood of innumerable war victims on their hands, they nevertheless chose to enshrine them alongside ordinary war dead. The aim was to rehabilitate war criminals, whitewash Japan's wartime atrocities, distort history, and pave the way for Japan's remilitarization. Takaichi pays lip service to peace while making offerings to war criminals. This pretense of peace is a blatant mockery of historical justice. For years before becoming prime minister, she repeatedly visited the Yasukuni Shrine. Since taking office, she has resorted to the more indirect approach of making ritual and monetary offerings -- a way of paying homage without visiting in person. She has used such tactics at least four times this year. On the one hand, she claims to champion peace and kneeled in Australia; on the other, she pays homage to the chief culprits behind Japanese militarists' war of aggression, denies the historical facts of the Nanjing Massacre, and upholds a distorted view of history. Her hypocrisy lays bare Japanese right-wing forces' determination to revive militarism and their underlying drive for aggression. Driven by this distorted view of history, Japan under Takaichi's leadership has continued to push beyond the constraints of the postwar system, with its militarist ambitions becoming increasingly brazen. In fiscal year 2026, Japan's defense budget exceeded 9 trillion yen (about $58 billion), marking 14 consecutive years of growth, with its expansion rate hitting a postwar record. Japan has fielded long-range missiles capable of striking enemy bases for the first time, fully relaxed restrictions on lethal weapons exports, and continued to erode its exclusively defense-oriented policy. It has also participated for the first time as a full member in the "Balikatan" joint military exercises by the Philippines and the U.S. It launched offensive shore-based anti-ship missiles overseas for the first time since World War II and pushed to rename the Air Self-Defense Force into "the Air and Space Self-Defense Force." Step by step, Japan is extending the reach of its so-called "security guarantees" overseas. No matter what "threats" Japanese politicians invoke as excuses, they cannot conceal their real aim of accelerating remilitarization and advancing its neo-militarism. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. In its solemn verdict, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East condemned Hideki Tojo and other Japanese Class-A war criminals to the lasting disgrace of history, upheld international justice, and laid the legal foundation for the postwar international order. Japanese leaders who visit or make offerings to the Yasukuni Shrine are, in essence, openly repudiating the verdicts of the Tokyo Trials, placing themselves against historical justice and the conscience of humanity, and challenging the victory of World War II and the postwar international order. The international community and people of conscience firmly oppose such actions. Spokespersons for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China and the Chinese Embassy in Japan have strongly condemned Japan's actions, urging the Japanese side to reflect deeply on its history of aggression, face up to its wartime crimes, and make a clean break with militarism. The South Korean government expressed "deep disappointment and regret," stressing that facing history squarely is a key foundation for building future-oriented relations between South Korea and Japan. Japanese scholars and intellectuals, including Masahiko Shimizu and Atsushi Koketsu, have pointed out that visits by Japanese politicians to the Yasukuni Shrine are wholly unacceptable from a historical standpoint and risk paving the way for another war of aggression. These reactions make clear that attempts to whitewash aggression and glorify war criminals are firmly rejected not only by the peoples of Asian countries that suffered under Japanese aggression, but also by peace-loving people within Japan itself. The evidence of Japanese militarism's crimes of aggression is overwhelming. History shall not be rewritten and justice must not be desecrated. If Japan continues to defy the tide of history and pursue its misguided course, it will once again find itself in the dock of history, condemned by the international community. (Zhong Sheng is a pen name often used by People's Daily to express its views on foreign policy and international relations.) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Chinese tech company unveils new AI model based on fully domestic computing power
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Chinese tech company unveils new AI model based on fully domestic computing power iFlytek 1024 Global Developer Festival 2026 is held in Beijing on October 22, 2026. Photo: Zhang Weilan/Global Times Chinese tech company iFlytek released and open-sourced its general-purpose large-language model (LLM), Spark-X2.6, at an industry event in Beijing on Thursday. The new model is an end-cloud integrated LLM that the company said has achieved breakthroughs in coding and agentic capabilities using fully domestic computing infrastructure. The model, sized at 293-A30B mixture-of-experts architecture (293B total parameters, 30B active per token), supports a context window of 1 million tokens and has been deployed on a domestic 10,000-card inference cluster. "Spark-X2.6 has taken the lead in breaking through the efficiency bottleneck of long-horizon task training on domestic chips, truly achieving independence and controllability with homegrown computing power," the company's chairperson Liu Qingfeng said at the iFlytek 1024 Global Developer Festival 2026 held in Beijing on Thursday. The company said that the model has reached performance levels comparable to leading industry systems in multiple technical benchmarks. However, Liu emphasized that the model's real-world deployment performance in actual industrial scenarios — such as state-owned enterprises, education, healthcare and judicial services — outperforms its public benchmark scores. An industry observer attending the event told the Global Times that the emphasis is shifting away from sheer model size and benchmark competition toward deployment on domestic computing, data security, and real-world usefulness in office, industrial and research settings. Liu Dingding, a veteran industry analyst, said that the combination of end-cloud collaboration and a fully domestic hardware base offers a reference path for China's artificial intelligence (AI) industry. "What matters next is whether a model can be rooted in a domestic computing foundation, balance efficiency with data security, and truly enter real scenarios of office work, industry and scientific research," Liu noted. The development also comes as ties between Chinese AI modelmakers and domestic chip suppliers deepen. According to domestic media reports, a research team led by the Shenzhen Loop Area Institute in South China's Guangdong Province has successfully used Huawei's Ascend 910C chips to complete post-training for the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model, marking a major step forward as China's semiconductor industry tries to leap from supporting basic AI inference to more complex model training. Liu said that tighter US restrictions on AI chip exports to China are increasing the strategic importance of domestic computing infrastructure, adding that closer collaboration between model developers and domestic chipmakers is pushing China's AI ecosystem from "usable" to "practical" and more mature. item.title: China issues revised administrative measures for outbound investment
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
China issues revised administrative measures for outbound investment BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China on Thursday unveiled revised administrative measures for outbound investment, aiming to provide stronger institutional safeguards for its development and security. The measures, released by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), China's top economic planner, will take effect on Dec. 1, 2026, replacing the existing rules enacted in 2017. The revision comes amid rapid growth in China's outbound investment and rising risks in an increasingly complex global environment, a spokesperson for the NDRC said. The revised measures further affirm the principal role of various investors in outbound investment, including domestic enterprises, individual residents, and other organizations. They also improve reporting systems for major adverse events and large overseas reinvestment projects, aiming to better protect the rights and interests of outbound investors and help them manage overseas risks. The revision is part of the country's broader efforts to promote the high-quality development of outbound investment. In June, China issued a new regulation on outbound investment, which calls for proactively aligning with high-standard international economic and trade rules, advancing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and promoting international cooperation in industrial and supply chains. China's outbound investment has continued to expand in recent years. By the end of 2025, the country's outbound investment stock had reached nearly 3.4 trillion U.S. dollars, keeping China among the world's top three investors for nine consecutive years, according to the Ministry of Commerce. The ministry also reported that China's outbound direct investment maintained steady and orderly growth, totaling 128.62 billion U.S. dollars in the first three quarters of 2026. item.title: China's top legislature to review draft law on Antarctic activities, environmental protection
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
China's top legislature to review draft law on Antarctic activities, environmental protection Zhao Leji, chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, presides over the 74th meeting of the Council of Chairpersons of the 14th NPC Standing Committee at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing) BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's top legislature will deliberate on the draft law on Antarctic activities and environmental protection during its upcoming session, marking the third review of the draft law. The enactment of the law was listed on the legislative plan of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee for 2026. The previous two reviews took place in December 2025 and June this year, respectively. The 14th NPC Standing Committee will hold its 25th session from Nov. 2 to 6, according to a Thursday meeting of the Council of Chairpersons of the standing committee presided over by NPC Standing Committee Chairman Zhao Leji. Apart from the draft law on Antarctic affairs, lawmakers at the session will review draft laws on public interest litigation by procuratorates, state-owned assets and finance, a draft law against cross-border corruption, and a draft revision to the Water Law. They will review bills for deliberation on a draft amendment to the Criminal Procedure Law, and draft revisions to the Renewable Energy Law and the Tax Collection Administration Law, among other draft amendments. A bill for deliberation on the ratification of the agreement on establishing the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization will also be reviewed at the session. item.title: Vietnamese student bridges China and Vietnam through traditional Chinese medicine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Vietnamese student bridges China and Vietnam through traditional Chinese medicine Vietnamese student Lam Quang Duong (L) practices acupuncture under the guidance of his mentor, Dr. Chen Manghua, at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine in Nanning, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Oct. 21, 2026. Lam enrolled to the university in 2019 and completed his undergraduate studies in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Now he is pursuing master degree in acupuncture and tuina. Coming from a family of medical professionals, he chose a different path from his family members, most of whom practice Western medicine. His goal was to become the first TCM practitioner in his family. Fluent in Chinese, Lam believes that TCM is not only a medical skill, but also a means of cross-border cultural exchange and heritage preservation. After graduation, he plans to return to Vietnam to practice medicine and continue his clinical and academic work in TCM. "I want to contribute to the medical development of China and Vietnam and help promote the exchange and preservation of traditional medicine between two countries," he said. item.title: "China Haul" reflects growing appeal of shopping in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
"China Haul" reflects growing appeal of shopping in China Foreign tourists select products at a Huawei flagship store in Beijing, capital of China, April 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong) BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's commerce ministry said that the "China Haul" trend on overseas social media reflects the rising recognition and appreciation of "Shopping in China." Yang Mu, head of the market operation and consumption promotion department of the Ministry of Commerce, said the phenomenon, depicting foreigners who share their experiences and joy of shopping in China on overseas social platforms, has also been a result of China's high-standard opening up and the charm of fine traditional Chinese culture. While commenting on booming inbound consumption at a press conference on Thursday, Yang said product categories favored by overseas consumers are expanding from traditional specialties such as tea and silk, previously the dominant choices, to tech gadgets, Chinese-style wellness products, beauty products and trendy toys. Shopping has become an important purpose of travel alongside sightseeing for overseas visitors, Yang said, adding that foreign visitors are now visiting more diverse corners of the country in addition to major cities. China continued to attract more foreign visitors in the third quarter of 2026, with visa-free entries rising 24.1 percent year on year to nearly 9 million. Visa-free entries accounted for 77.5 percent of all entries by foreign nationals during the period, official data showed. Building on the country's continued expansion of visa-free arrangements, a series of policy measures have also been rolled out to make shopping in China easier, including upgraded tax refund policies. From January to August this year, nationwide departure tax refund sales increased by about 60 percent year on year, and the number of people receiving tax refunds rose by 300 percent. At present, there are more than 18,000 tax refund stores nationwide, an increase of 400 percent compared with the end of 2024, official data showed. Yang said that going forward, the ministry will work to improve the "Shopping in China" experience by enriching high-quality supply, expanding the coverage of departure tax refunds, and improving payment-related services. item.title: China issues first policy document dedicated to technology-driven commerce
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
China issues first policy document dedicated to technology-driven commerce Humanoid robots handle production materials in a workshop of a mechanical and electrical company in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Long Wei) A new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is gathering pace. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, embodied intelligence and digital twins are evolving rapidly, reshaping how commerce is organized and operated while improving the consumer experience. By harnessing technology, businesses can expand the supply of goods and services, create more diverse consumption scenarios and reduce the cost of consumer decision-making, while making distribution and circulation more efficient and lowering logistics costs. These advances can help bring supply and demand into dynamic balance at a higher level. China recently released new guidelines on accelerating technology-driven commerce, its first policy document dedicated to this subject. Yuan Xiaoming, assistant minister of commerce, said the comprehensive and systematic guidelines were formulated in light of the requirements of China's new stage of development. They place technological innovation at the heart of the entire commerce chain and seek to promote deeper integration between technology and commerce. Their key features can be summed up in three words: new, comprehensive and practical. "New" means putting technological innovation at the forefront and responding to emerging consumption trends and changing consumer preferences. As living standards rise, consumers are paying greater attention to product quality and the overall consumption experience. Data from the Ministry of Commerce showed that sales of smart glasses on major platforms rose 110 percent year on year in the first nine months of this year. The widespread application of AI, the Internet of Things and blockchain in the consumer sector has made technological innovation an increasingly important driver of consumption growth and upgrading. A consumer browses new-model smartphones at a shopping mall in Leshan, southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo/Li Huashi) The guidelines respond to the latest developments in science and technology and industrial transformation. They address the immediate need to expand consumption and invigorate the consumer market, while looking to the longer term by using technological innovation to upgrade traditional commerce and foster emerging business models, injecting sustained momentum into high-quality commercial development. "Comprehensive" means pursuing progress on both the supply and demand sides and covering the entire commerce chain and all business formats. Vertically, the guidelines integrate technological innovation into every stage of commerce, from product research and development, manufacturing and service provision on the supply side to wholesale, logistics, e-commerce and the final consumption experience. Horizontally, they promote the technological upgrading of traditional businesses such as retail, catering and housekeeping to revitalize traditional consumption, while fostering new business models and formats, including commercial AI agents and green, circular consumption, to unlock the potential of emerging forms of consumption. Together, these measures establish a comprehensive policy framework that coordinates supply and demand and promotes both traditional and new forms of consumption. "Practical" means focusing on real-world problems and ensuring that policies can be implemented and their results assessed. The guidelines target pressing issues in commerce with tailored measures. To better match the supply of goods with consumer demand, for example, they call for developing flexible manufacturing, promoting on-demand production and fostering a number of influential customized brands. To expand the supply of high-quality services, they propose accelerating the digital and intelligent transformation of services related to housekeeping, healthcare, elderly care and childcare, while developing upgraded services such as smart education, smart cultural tourism and smart sports. To drive the upgrading of goods supply, China will further implement its special initiative on "AI + Manufacturing." Estimates show that the scale of China's core AI industry exceeded 1.2 trillion yuan ($179.69 billion) in 2025. An unmanned delivery vehicle runs on a rural road in Jinping county, southwest China's Guizhou province. (Photo/Yang Xiaohai) Intelligent products and services are now becoming increasingly widespread: AI-powered smartphones are finding their way into people's pockets, intelligent connected vehicles are taking to the roads, and humanoid robots are moving into factories. In the first half of this year, shipments of various smart terminals exceeded 100 million units. In the first half of the year, the number of humanoid robot models in China exceeded 400, while output surpassed 40,000 units. To expand the supply of upgraded services, China will launch pilot applications of AI in culture and tourism. Zhou Hanping, an official with the Department of Industrial Development at the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, said that a number of museums, cultural venues and tourist attractions are leveraging technologies such as digital twins, extended reality and ultra-high-definition imaging to bring cultural resources to life. In this way, artifacts long kept out of public view and the stories of history are being transformed into cultural and tourism experiences that visitors can see, participate in and connect with emotionally. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism has selected and approved 14 projects for the pilot applications. These projects will help build experience and pave the way for successful practices to be rolled out nationwide. Advancing technology-driven commerce requires the participation of businesses and organizations across the entire sector. It is a collective endeavor in which large enterprises build platforms, develop key technologies and set examples, while small and medium-sized enterprises adopt digital tools, access services and explore new markets. By playing to their respective strengths and finding their place in the broader ecosystem, businesses of all sizes can share the benefits of technology-driven commerce. Yuan said the Ministry of Commerce would work with other government departments to ensure that the guidelines are effectively implemented and that the potential of technological innovation is translated into tangible momentum for commercial development. item.title: Xiplomacy: Reading Xi's vision for global governance through metaphors
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Xiplomacy: Reading Xi's vision for global governance through metaphors An aerial drone photo taken on Aug. 4, 2026 shows a view of the Nanhe water conservancy hub in Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province. (Xinhua/Mu Yu) BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) is set to open on Friday in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, bringing into world focus a pressing question: How can countries work together to address shared challenges in an interconnected world amid growing protectionism and unilateralism? In speeches and meetings on multiple occasions, Chinese President Xi Jinping has used vivid metaphors to articulate his vision for global governance. These metaphors offer insights into his approach to building a more just, equitable and inclusive global governance system. IN SAME BOAT "I was looking at the vast ocean when I boarded the ship, and it struck me that we are all indeed fellow passengers in the same boat," Xi said while addressing the 2018 APEC CEO Summit hosted at a unique setting -- onboard the giant cruise Pacific Explorer in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea. The metaphor embodies the essence of Xi's vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, highlighting the interconnectedness of countries and the need for solidarity and cooperation in addressing common challenges. Today, the interconnected world is grappling with four mounting deficits: a peace deficit that exacerbates geopolitical conflicts, a development deficit that widens the North-South divide, a security deficit that erodes mutual trust, and a governance deficit that undermines the effectiveness of multilateralism. This photo taken on Aug. 30, 2025 shows an exterior view of the main venue of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2025 in Tianjin, north China. (Xinhua/Sun Fanyue) In 2019, at the China-France Global Governance Forum held in Paris, Xi proposed a four-pronged approach to addressing the four deficits. First and foremost, he called for fairness and reasonableness to address the governance deficit. "It is advisable to uphold a vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefits," Xi said, calling for actively advancing the democratization of global governance rules. As the world has found itself in a new period of turbulence and transformation, global governance has come to a new crossroads. Against this backdrop, Xi put forward the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in September 2025 in China's coastal city of Tianjin. "I look forward to working with all countries for a more just and equitable global governance system and advancing toward a community with a shared future for humanity," Xi said, stressing sovereign equality and genuine multilateralism. TRAFFIC LIGHTS "A world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed," Xi said at the 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India. This metaphor highlights the importance of rules in maintaining the international order. While having rules in place matters, how they are made and who gets to make them matter even more. Media staff work at the media center at Bharat Mandapam, the main venue of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Javed Dar) International rules must be written and upheld jointly by all countries based on the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, rather than dictated by those with the strongest muscles or the loudest voice, Xi once stressed. He has also called for the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and other universally recognized basic norms of international relations to be observed comprehensively, fully and in their entirety. "There should be no double standards, and the house rules of a few countries must not be imposed upon others," he said. The GGI proposed by President Xi reflects the objective transformation of the world system and responds to the aspirations of most countries for a fairer and more representative system of global governance, said Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University. MAKING THE PIE BIGGER Xi has repeatedly used the metaphor of a pie to describe the gains of international cooperation. "We should make the pie of win-win cooperation bigger, and ensure that more development gains will be shared more fairly by people across the world," he said at the 23rd meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in 2023. The pie metaphor reflects the people-centered and action-oriented vision of the GGI: making the gains of cooperation bigger while ensuring that they are shared more widely and fairly. When proposing the GGI, Xi emphasized the importance of "ensuring that the people of every nation are the actors in and beneficiaries of global governance." Students operate teaching equipment for the artificial intelligence program at the Luban Workshop at L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University in Astana, Kazakhstan, May 22, 2026. (Photo by Kalizhan Ospanov/Xinhua) The SCO, the platform where Xi proposed the GGI, provides an example. Within the grouping, China has announced the establishment of cooperation platforms in energy, green industries and the digital economy, as well as centers for scientific and technological innovation, higher education, and vocational and technical education. The expanding scope of cooperation shows how the "pie" can be made bigger in practice: by opening up new areas of cooperation, creating more opportunities for development and ensuring that the benefits reach more people. Beyond making the pie bigger, Xi has also called for sharing the pie fairly to ensure justice and equity. For him, the ultimate purpose of better global governance is to promote common development and improve people's well-being across the globe. At the G20 summit held in Brazil in 2024, Xi called for building a just world of common development, saying "prosperity and stability would not be possible in a world where the rich become richer while the poor are made poorer, and countries should make global development more inclusive, beneficial to all, and more resilient." To build such a world, Xi said, there should be more bridges of cooperation, and less "small yard, high fences," so that more and more developing countries will be better off and achieve modernization. item.title: Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting to review disciplinary inspection report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting to review disciplinary inspection report BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee held a meeting on Friday to review a report on the seventh round of disciplinary inspection launched by the 20th CPC Central Committee. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, chaired the meeting. The meeting hailed the work performance and results of the inspection. According to the inspection results, central Party and government departments have made progress in their work, but some problems still exist and need to be taken seriously. The meeting urged solid efforts to rectify the problems identified by the inspection. It called on central Party and government departments to strengthen their sense of political responsibility in performing their duties, deepen reform, and ensure both development and security. It also stressed the need to strengthen leadership teams, while adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. The meeting also discussed other matters. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
